rationale: The analysis stage showed that a parallel comparison of 11 boards has about 40 percent power, and licensing allows only two boards per wave. The network's six-wave schedule is itself the better design: a pragmatic stepped-wedge cluster trial in which the order of boards is set by chance within strata of board size, so every board contributes before and after periods and every board has the template by December 2027. Planning values come from claims c1 and c4; time to first treatment (claim c3) and meeting duration (claim c5) are secondary and balancing outcomes. Secular trends are modelled, and the four boards affected by the information system merger are placed in waves away from June to August 2027. Reporting follows the CONSORT extension for stepped-wedge cluster trials.
alternatives: Parallel cluster comparison with five boards starting in December (superseded: about 40 percent power and not allowed by licensing)
Before-after comparison across the network (refused: cannot separate the package from secular change)
guidelines: CONSORT extension for stepped-wedge cluster randomised trials
whyNotMoreComplex: Randomising individual case discussions is impossible because the template is switched on per board; a stepped-wedge design uses the schedule the network already needs.

decision.statement: Run a pragmatic stepped-wedge cluster trial on the network's six-wave schedule: the order in which the 11 boards join the waves is set by chance within strata of board size, every board has the template by December 2027, documentation completeness is the primary outcome and secular trends are modelled.
decision.question: Does the template package increase complete decision documentation, and shorten time to first treatment without lengthening meetings?

criteria.text: With 11 boards, the stepped design has adequate power where a parallel design does not.
Meeting time and time to treatment can be measured as balancing and secondary outcomes.
The information system merger removes data for the four affected boards for longer than two months.

gates.requirement: Research ethics approval covering the evaluation, with every board receiving the template in 2027
gates.evidence: Approval REB-CN-2026-118 dated 2026-08-29, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Network board approval of the six-wave rollout
gates.evidence: Network board minute NB-2026-06-11, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Parallel cluster comparison with a December start for five boards (superseded)
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1, c3, c4 and c5 from retrieved records; both gates rest on the investigator's records. Supersedes the parallel design.

summary: Pragmatic stepped-wedge trial recommended; it supersedes the parallel design and both gates are met.
